memos.risk:
Risk call: this brief is a weak setup, and I'd refuse to size it.

The curve data is alarming. bundle_share is 1.0 and top3_share is 0.988, meaning essentially all early supply moved through bundled wallets and the top three holders control nearly everything. completer_share above 1 is also a red flag. Only 4 buyers are listed on the curve against 546 ex-agent buyers in the first two minutes, which points to a bundle/operator structure rather than organic demand. Post-graduation sells are 78% of buys, and the last 15 minutes show net outflow of 22 SOL with 954 sellers.

The positives (alive, 30-minute return of +25%, 17% drawdown from the high, a 138 SOL pool) don't outweigh this. Operator-backed coins have broken even on average, and a bundled curve with this sell pressure is a dump setup.

Refuse any size. If the desk later wants a looser look, the minimum conditions would be a broken-up top-3 holder share and sustained positive net flow, which this brief doesn't show. Skipping costs nothing.
memos.scout: The strongest honest case rests on the last 15 minutes: 2,238 buyers pushed in 518 SOL against 496 SOL sold, with 954 sellers. That is real two-sided turnover, not a dump, and the coin is still up 18% over that window and 25% over 30 minutes. Launch-day supply was not airdropped (airdrop_dump_seen: false), and the first two minutes show 546 external buyers against a 0.78 sell-to-buy ratio, so early selling was not overwhelming. Pool depth of 138 SOL is deep enough that a $20 ticket won't be swallowed by impact. Counterweights are real, though: bundle_share of 1.0 and top-3 curve share of 98.8% point to coordinated early buying, and the 17% drawdown from the 30-minute high means momentum is already fading. Net flow of only 22 SOL over 15 minutes is thin against that turnover. The case is modest, and the entry is late. Without a clear reason demand holds for another 30 to 60 minutes, I would not buy.
memos.skeptic:
The most likely way this loses is insider distribution into the retail flow. The curve data is a red flag: bundle_share is 1.0 and top3_share is 0.988, meaning nearly all early supply was taken by bundled wallets, and completer_share of 1.17 suggests the curve was completed by those same insiders. In the first two minutes after graduation, the sell-to-buy ratio was 0.78 and the top 5 buyers held 45% of volume, so early holders are already positioned to exit.

Recent flow shows the same pattern: over the last 15 minutes, 496 SOL sold against 518 SOL bought, with net flow only 22 SOL on about 2,200 buyers and 954 sellers. The 17% drawdown from the 30-minute high, despite a 25% gain over 30 minutes, is consistent with the bundle beginning to sell. With a 137.9 SOL pool and a 1.4-5.1% round trip cost, a 17% reversal erases any small upside, and the base rate for random buys of alive coins like this is roughly 20% loss per trade. Skip.
